item.title: Cowboys vs. Packers live updates, inactives, where to watch: Dak Prescott, Jordan Love face off on 'Sunday Night Football' in Week 6
item.description: The Cowboys and Packers close out the Sunday slate in Week 6.
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers will close out the Week 6 NFL Sunday slate in primetime, with kickoff set for 8:20 p.m. ET at Lambeau Field.

The Cowboys enter Week 6 at 2-3, but with a wide-open NFC East, as each of the teams within the division has struggled. The New York Giants fell 34-27 to the New Orleans Saints in the early Sunday window, while the Eagles fell to the Carolina Panthers without quarterback Jalen Hurts, who wound up on injured reserve this week with a blood clot in his leg. As the defense continues to struggle this season, the pressure falls on Dak Prescott & Co. on offense to make some magic.

The Packers enter this game two games back from the undefeated Minnesota Vikings after a slow start to the season. They bounced back in a big way, however, with a dominant divisional win over the Chicago Bears last week, where quarterback Jordan Love showed off his skills with the deep ball, featuring Christian Watson and Matthew Golden as key weapons in the passing game.

Absent from this matchup is star defensive end Micah Parsons, who continues his recovery from a torn ACL last season. Though he was targeting a Week 6 return against his former team, he’s yet to be activated to the roster and practice with the team this season.

Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the Green Bay Packers host the Dallas Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football" in Week 6.

item.title: Jim Harbaugh on Mike McDaniel: We'll look at everything, offense needs to be addressed
item.description: McDaniel could be dismissed as offensive coordinator after an 0-6 start.
item.content:encoded:
The Chargers failed to score a touchdown in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs and they head into their bye week under increased speculation about whether offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel will still be on the staff when they return in Week 8.

PFT reported "growing buzz" on Sunday that the Chargers will be parting ways with McDaniel after the team fell to 0-6 since putting him in charge of the offense. The Chargers have scored just 84 points in those six losses, which is a far cry from what many expected when McDaniel was hired to work with quarterback Justin Herbert in the offseason. Herbert threw his eighth interception on Sunday and has thrown at least one in each of the futile offensive performances.

After Sunday's loss, head coach Jim Harbaugh was asked if McDaniel will be calling the plays when the team returns against the Rams in two weeks.

"We're going to look at everything. . . . I feel bad for our players, our team, our coaches, our fans. And (the offense) needs to be addressed," Harbaugh said, via Noah Furtado of TheAthletic.com.

If the Chargers do make a move with McDaniel, former Jets head coach and current pass game specialist Adam Gase is expected to take over the offensive reins.

item.title: Jordan Love touchdown pass gives Packers 7-0 lead over Cowboys
item.description: Dallas’ defense still looks porous to start Sunday night’s game against Green Bay.
item.content:encoded:
Dallas’ defense still looks porous to start Sunday night’s game against Green Bay.

Packers quarterback Jordan Love connected with receiver Matthew Golden for a 9-yard touchdown, giving the club a 7-0 lead.

The 14-play, 90-yard drive took 6:30 off the clock.

Though the Packers didn’t really get anything going on the ground, Jordan Love moved it just fine through the air. He was 6-of-8 for 109 yards with a TD to open the contest. Two penalties moved Green Bay back, allowing for that yardage on what was technically a 90-yard possession.

Golden caught the touchdown and had a big 37-yard catch to move the chains — though he was flagged for taunting. Christian Watson also had a 27-yard reception on the possession.

Green Bay was 4-of-4 on third down.

The Cowboys had to punt to end their first possession after gaining one first down.

Dallas returner KaVontae Turpin has a rib injury and is questionable to return. He was hurt on the opening kickoff. Tyler Goodson has come in to replace Turpin as a kickoff returner.

item.title: Josh Allen, Buffalo Bills, now 5-1, finding ways to win close games
item.description: Josh Allen and the 5-1 Buffalo Bills continue making the right sort of magic happen in the biggest moments of shootouts
item.content:encoded:
It’s no secret that Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is a superbly talented, generational player. With Allen, the Bills are always well-positioned to win every game at any moment. Yet, winning in the NFL is difficult. It’s true that the mark of a great team isn’t necessarily how dominant it performs in a blowout win, but how well they play in a close victory.

For Buffalo a third of the way through the 2026 NFL season, the title of “Finishers” suits them well. All but one game (a win vs. Detroit Lions Week 2 — 41-31) has come down to a single score’s difference. Wins against the Houston Texans in Week 1 (36-31), Los Angeles Chargers Week 3 (24-16), Los Angeles Rams Week 5 (37-34), and Las Vegas Raiders Week 6 (33-30) took all the mental fortitude, discipline, and dialed-in play they could muster in all three phases.

Their only loss this season, also decided by a single score — 29-26 to the New England Patriots in Week 3 — further reveals that these Bills may play a heck of a lot more games in similar fashion. It’s possible that Buffalo’s remaining schedule finds them in high-scoring shootouts where even 30 points doesn’t feel as comfortable as one might expect.

Allen is obviously a huge reason why the Bills win the games they do, especially when he’s good for at least one impossibly brilliant play at the goal line for six. However, he’s not the only one on that side of the ball who makes Buffalo a feared team.

Running back James Cook III is a special player. He again played a key role in victory, finishing with 22 carries for 95 yards and a score, plus three catches for 58 yards. Better yet? Cook didn’t fumble, as I predicted he’d rebound with a strong performance.

Then there’s wide receiver Keon Coleman, who’s really turned it on in year three. The Bills needed Coleman to step up when top wide receiver DJ Moore picked up a shoulder injury, and Coleman has impressed. He’s beginning to look like a receiver ready for a consistent spotlight, with hands fit for carrying diamonds across tight ropes and verticality for days.

To address the pink elephant in the room: Yes, the defense is yet a work in progress, and will be so well into training camp next summer with defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard at the helm. That said, the defensive line and edge rushers are bigger disruptors now, and so many holdover players are more efficient in almost every scenario.

As for the defensive backfield? The masterful play by top cornerback Christian Benford against tight end Brock Bowers can’t be over-discussed in the coming days. Bowers, of course, had a decent day — but only when going against anyone not named Benford, and most folks will sign up for four catches and 70 yards without a score going up against Bowers.

CBS game analyst J.J. Watt pointed out Benford’s play several times, saying that he should be the only one covering Bowers. In key moments where Bowers was likely to have the biggest impact, Benford was his shadow playing expertly blanketed coverage. The hope is that Buffalo’s other defensive backs use Benford’s tape in Week 6 to raise their individual levels to the greater good.

To be fair, the defense played much better in Las Vegas. There will always be those ready to bash even the slightest mistake out of Jim Leonhard’s group. That’s just life. There’s also lot of good to focus on out of the ashes of yet another close victory that might not have been so without more than a few key defensive stops.

Were there moments where it appeared Buffalo couldn’t do a thing to stop Las Vegas’ passing attack? Certainly. Expecting a finished product at this point is foolish. The defense has made strides in pass coverage, and the difference in run defense is night and day compared to former head coach Sean McDermott’s system.

Buffalo needed its defense to step up today, and it did just enough at the right moments to give Allen, Cook, and company a path to victory. For that alone, a toast should be raised toward a Bills stop unit so often under the microscope.

Winning close games will better prepare this young team for a postseason run. They just have to keep winning to put that theory to a proper test.

item.title: Caleb Williams "just let it rip" in his return from hamstring tear
item.description: Caleb Williams had one question for the media as he made his way into the tunnel toward the visiting locker room.
item.content:encoded:
Caleb Williams had one question for the media as he made his way into the tunnel toward the visiting locker room.

"Y’all like that?" Williams asked rhetorically, smiling, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN.

The Bears quarterback returned after missing three games with a torn hamstring. He completed his first 12 passes and finished 30-of-36 for 305 yards and a touchdown.

"I felt confident from the jump," Williams said. "When I get out there, I'm going to feel confident in my leg, in myself and in my guys and the O-line. So I just let it rip, let these guys go make plays for us, get first downs and score touchdowns."

The Bears now have a quick turnaround, with a Thursday night game against the Patriots looming.

Despite four sacks, Williams said he is no worse for wear in his first game back.

"Felt great to get hit after three weeks of just rehabbing," Williams said. "So [I] feel strong, feel good. Obviously got to go and take care of it this week. It's going to be a weekly thing, just taking care of it, staying up to date on it and taking care of my body."

item.title: Omar Cooper Jr. hits triple digits in Week 6 vs. Patriots
item.description: New England Patriots wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. had six receptions for 103 yards and a touchdown on a team-high seven targets in Week 6
item.content:encoded:
New England Patriots wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. had six receptions for 103 yards and a touchdown on a team-high seven targets in Week 6 against the New England Patriots.

SOURCE: USA TODAY

Why it Matters: The rookie out of Indiana had a breakout game in his first game back after a month-long recovery from an ankle injury. He is going to be a popular pick-up off of the waiver wire this week, but proceed with caution. Garrett Wilson is still the top dog for Gang Green, and Cooper should be treated as a WR5 for now.

item.title: Former Broncos G.M. John Beake dies at 87
item.content:encoded:
Former Broncos G.M. John Beake recently died. He was 87.

Beake, pictured with former Broncos coach Dan Reeves, spent 22 years with the Denver organization. He served as the General Manager until 2000.

"The Broncos are saddened by the passing of longtime executive John Beake, who made an enduring impact on our organization during more than two decades with the team," the Broncos said in a statement. "John helped guide the Broncos to five Super Bowl appearances, including back-to-back World Championships, and was a respected leader throughout one of the most successful eras in franchise history. Following his time in Denver, he remained an influential figure through his work with the NFL and on the Broncos Ring of Fame Committee. Our deepest condolences are with his wife, Marcia, his sons, Chip and Chris, and the entire Beake family."

Before joining the Broncos in 1979, he worked as an assistant coach with the Chiefs from 1968 to 1974 and the Saints from 1976 through 1977. Beake was on Hank Stram's coaching staff when Kansas City won Super Bowl IV.

After leaving the Broncos, Beake worked for the league office.

item.title: Cardinals send reeling Rams to 2-4 and in danger of missing the playoffs with late rally aided by controversial penalty
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams entered the season as favorites to win the Super Bowl. Through six weeks of the NFL season, they look like anything but after another tough-luck loss.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams entered the season as favorites to win the Super Bowl. Through six weeks of the NFL season, they look like anything but, and are in danger of missing the playoffs.

The Rams dropped to 2-4 on Sunday with a stunning 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals that drops them well out of the race in the NFC West, and leaves them with an uphill battle to get into wild-card contention.

Like the Rams' Week 3 loss to the Denver Broncos, this one was not without officiating controversy.

After trailing for most of the game, the Rams drove 86 yards on eight plays to secure a 16-15 lead with 47 seconds remaining in regulation. The Cardinals started their ensuing possession at their own 35-yard line following a touchback.

Should this have been unnecessary roughness?

A 21-yard pass from Jacoby Brissett to Jalen Brooks on the first play of the drive moved the ball across midfield, and a questionable unnecessary roughness penalty on the hit added 15 yards to the gain.

Jalen Brooks takes a huge shot and pops right back up#ARIvsLARpic.twitter.com/kR9MsrLKd4

— crunchypuddle (@crunchypuddle1) October 18, 2026

Rams cornerback Josh Wallace was in zone coverage on the play and waiting to make a hit on Brooks after the receiver leapt in the air to make the catch.

As Brooks landed, his helmet made grazing contact with Wallace's shoulder pad. Wallace leaned in to make the hit, but contact was minimal. The call of a personal foul was questionable at best.

WOW... Rams get called for a personal foul for hitting a defenseless receiver... he barely touched him but the refs added 15 yards to the end of this play for that pic.twitter.com/6xuLynSAiw

— Rate the Refs (@Rate_the_Refs) October 18, 2026

That play and penalty set the Cardinals up with 1st-and-10 at the Los Angeles 29-yard line. It ultimately set Chad Ryland up for a 43-yard game-winning field goal as time expired.

CHAD RYLAND WINS IT FOR THE CARDINALS pic.twitter.com/QfTHlvwVcr

— NFL (@NFL) October 18, 2026

It added up to another tough-luck loss for the Rams, but they didn't look good throughout Sunday's game.

Rams struggled throughout Sunday's game

An offense that entered Sunday leading the NFL in yards per game was ineffective against a Cardinals defense that entered the game ranked 26th in the league.

With left tackle Alaric Jackson suspended due to his postgame punch of Bradley Chubb last week, Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford was under pressure early and often, and the Rams struggled to gain any traction in the passing game until their late drive to take the 16-15 lead.

The Cardinals sacked Stafford three times and hit him five more. He was under consistent pressure even when he wasn't getting hit. The result was a Rams offense that managed just one touchdown and nine points through the game's first 59-plus minutes.

The Rams had 107 yards at halftime and finished with 286 for the game.

Late go-ahead drive not enough for Rams

That final tally and Stafford's final stat line (25 of 33, 222 yards, 2 TDs, 0 INTs) were salvaged by the late 86-yard touchdown drive that featured completions of 16 and 43 yards from Stafford to Puka Nacua. Tight end Colby Parkinson stretched for a score on a short pass from Stafford to ensure that the drive to the red zone paid off.

COLBY STRETCHES IT IN!

📺: @NFLonFOX | #RamsHousepic.twitter.com/oXR31h9iOk

— Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) October 18, 2026

But it wasn't enough to secure a Rams win.

In the end, the Rams didn't score enough points to beat an Arizona team that picked up its second win of the season. Now both teams are tied at the bottom of the NFC West at 2-4, well behind the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers, who play the Commanders on Monday Night Football. And the Cardinals have the edge in the standings thanks to the head-to-head win.

Davante Adams left late with injury

Making matters worse for the Rams, they leave the game with injury concerns on multiple fronts. All-Pro receiver Davante Adams came up limping on the game's final drive with what looked like a non-contact leg injury.

Davante Adams non contact injury? pic.twitter.com/AeqOLUnW8D

— Savage (@Savageboston) October 18, 2026

He did not return to the game. His status was unclear in the game's immediate aftermath.

And the Rams lost new kicker Blake Grupe to a knee injury in the first quarter, leaving them without a kicker and in precarious positions throughout the game. The Rams signed Grupe to replace Harrison Mevis, whom they cut after Monday's 37-34 loss to the Bills.

They went for two points and failed after a second-quarter touchdown to limit their lead to 9-6. They went for it on 4th-and-1 at the Arizona 27-yard line in the second half instead of attempting a game-tying 44-yard field goal. They failed to get the first down and turned the ball over on downs.

When they scored their late touchdown to tie the game at 15-15, punter Ethan Evans successfully kicked the extra point to momentarily give the Rams the lead.

The Rams have winnable upcoming games against Raiders, Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals again. But Sunday's game at home was also supposed to be winnable.

And while the loss was aided by a controversial penalty in the final seconds, it was poor play throughout the game from the Los Angeles offense that put the Rams in position to lose to begin with.
